investigations.question: D5 RETRY, EVIDENCE-ONLY, HARD CAP 300 WORDS. Prove the strongest rigorous lower bound currently attainable for N(H), the number of sorted solutions (a,b,c,d), 1<=a<=b<=c<=d, of a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=4abcd with d<=H. No introduction, no tables, no prose motivation. Cite as frozen facts, without reproving: the quotient graph is a tree rooted at v0=(1,1,1,1); children of a non-root are the distinct sorted vertices obtained by mutating a,b,c; child maximum is at most 4d^3 (answer:work:003-struct-core-v2, answer:work:004-upper-depth-v3). Prove exactly these lemmas. L1 CHAIN: with (c1,d1)=(1,3), c_{j+1}=d_j, d_{j+1}=4d_j-c_j, prove v_j=(1,1,c_j,d_j) are distinct solutions, d_{j+1}=4d_j-d_{j-1}, d0=1,d1=3, lambda=2+sqrt(3), and d_j = A lambda^j + B lambda^{-j} with A=(3+sqrt(3))/6, B=(3-sqrt(3))/6, hence d_j<=lambda^j and N(H)>=floor(log_lambda H)+1. L2 TWO CHILDREN BELOW DEPTH 2: at a vertex with at least two distinct values among a,b,c, the child maxima f(x)=4abcd/x-x are distinct because f is strictly decreasing; if a=b=c=x, prove from x|d and d=kx that k^2+3=4kx^2, k|3, and the only possibilities are the root or v1=(1,1,1,3). Therefore every vertex at depth >=2 has at least two distinct children. L3 BINARY SUBTREE: below v2=(1,1,3,11), use child max <=4d^3. If A=log2(11)+1, after t edges log2(d)<=3^t A. Thus whenever 3^t A<=log2(H), all 2^t vertices at that level below v2 have d<=H. Take t=floor(log_3(log2(H)/A)), beta=log_3 2=0.6309, c'=1/(2A^beta) (approximately 0.194), H>=32, and conclude N(H)>=c'(log2 H)^beta. FINAL LINE: N(H)>=max(floor(log_{2+sqrt3} H)+1, c'(log2 H)^0.6309) for H>=32, with the polylogarithmic term asymptotically dominant. Anything stronger must be labeled CONJECTURE with the exact missing lemma.
